Its own head population (logs/head-population.log, -n 4) ends '4 failed, 158 passed' EXIT=1; every one of those four is reproduced by the run's own base arms and none reaches the covered-set code this node changed. logs/base-window.log fails tests/test_every_module_fits_a_worker_window.py at the base revision on reckon/roadmap.py's 51232-token estimate, and logs/head-population.log fails the same test at head and touches no file this node changed. findings.text: follow-on: `_reuse_covered` now returns a third element, `bool(moved)`, and every caller discards it — `index_rows` binds it to `_scanned` and never reads it (metadata_index.py:368), `_covered_files` uses `reused[0]` (metadata_index.py:756) and `reckon/resources.py:802` uses `reused[0]` too — so the value and the three-line docstring paragraph that describes what the third element reports are dead API. Nothing measures the signal, so a future reader who trusts the docstring learns nothing from it.

follow-on: the manifest names no baseline_suite and no after_suite line, so the reviewed run's own suite arm pair — the two logs the review contract derives an added-failure count from — is absent and the count had to fall back to the gate logs named in test_logs. The run does name base arms (base-cold-read.log, base-window.log, base-page-paints-alone.log) and a head population of the same readers, so the evidence exists; it is the manifest fields that do not carry it, and a reader rebuilding my derivation from my record's own citation finds no pair to reduce.
